title: SLO threshold spike and decision log for model-serving endpoints
linked_artifacts: JIRA-RI-987: SLO Baselines for Hosted API
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a time-boxed technical spike to propose concrete SLO threshold options for model-serving endpoints, and an explicit decision log for selecting and operationalizing thresholds. Goal is to produce a recommendation that is implementable by the infra and serving teams and testable via canary rollouts in Dedicated/Hosted.

Context / Why now:
- Product teams are asking for stricter latency promises for chat endpoints; infra costs and region variability complicate choosing a single global threshold.
- We need a quick, defensible path from observed telemetry to an SLO that balances customer experience with sustainable error budgets.
- This spike sits between research (observability, A/B signal analysis) and ops (runbooks, rollback triggers).

Hypothesis:
- Using a two-tier SLO (p50 latency for UX signal + p95 latency guardrail) yields better tradeoffs than a single p95 SLO for model-serving in most customer workloads.
- A 350ms p50 + 1.2s p95 threshold for short-chat requests (<=128 tokens) will keep UX good while keeping error budgets manageable on current Dedicated pools.

Scope (30-day spike):
- Measure: gather 90 days of production telemetry for endpoints: p50/p75/p95 latency, tail latency distribution, 4xx/5xx rates, kv-cache hit ratios, CPU/GPU utilization correlated to latency events.
- Run controlled load tests and a canary ramp in one region (us-west1) across three model sizes (small/medium/large equivalents).
- Produce decision matrix and runbook snippets (alerts, canary gating, rollback triggers).
- Deliverable: single-page recommendation + decision log + checklist for rollout.

Data sources / queries to run (notes to self):
- Observability dashboards: slo-latency-model-serving (prometheus + traces).
- Query: histograms of request durations by request_type, model_size, token_count_bucket.
- Export: top 5 stack traces correlated with tail latency >95th.
- Ask telemetry team for raw samples for 2026-08..2026-11.

Experiment plan (high level):
1) Baseline analysis (days 1–5): produce latency distributions by segment (token_count, model, route).
2) Load spike tests (days 6–12): synthetic traffic with realistic prefix distributions (use replay tool). Capture cache warmup effects.
3) Canary ramp (days 13–20): route 1% -> 5% -> 15% traffic on hosted API to a config with batch size tweaks and KV cache warming. Monitor: p50/p95, error rate, GPU queue length, request timeouts.
4) Post-mortem and threshold selection (days 21–25): feed results into decision matrix.
5) Runbook draft & stakeholder review (days 26–30).

Key metrics to collect (minimum):
- p50, p75, p90, p95, p99 request latency (mgmt by token_count buckets: 0-64, 65-128, 129-512, >512).
- Request success rate (2xx vs 4xx/5xx), timeout count, retry count.
- Error budget consumption rate (per 7-day and 28-day windows).
- GPU utilization, queue depth, avg batch size, KV cache hit rate.
- Customer-visible latencies (SDK median perceived time including network).

Decision criteria (ranked):
1) UX impact: % of requests with perceived delay > 500ms for short chat.
2) Error budget sustainability: projected monthly burn if threshold adopted.
3) Operational overhead: need for autoscale / burst capacity / manual ops.
4) Rollback complexity and risk.

Initial candidate thresholds to evaluate (short-chat <=128 tokens):
- Conservative: p50 <= 250ms, p95 <= 900ms (low UX risk, high infra cost)
- Balanced (our prior guess): p50 <= 350ms, p95 <= 1.2s (good UX, manageable cost)
- Aggressive: p50 <= 200ms, p95 <= 700ms (very expensive, may require reserved capacity)

Runbook and canary gating (prototype snippets):
- Canary gating rule (per region): abort rollout if p95 > threshold *or* error-rate increases by >50% over baseline for 15m rolling.
- Escalation: SRE on-call + serving-runtime owner if error budget burn rate > 5%/hr for 3 consecutive hours.
- Automated fallback: route new requests to smaller model variant or pre-quantized variant if queue depth > X and p95 breaches.

Decision log (chronological entries) — use this to capture why we pick thresholds:
- 2026-11-30: Spike created by Riley Chen. Hypothesis documented (two-tier SLO).
- 2026-12-02: Baseline queries ran. Note: p95 for small models in us-west1 peaked at 1.05s on median weekdays; tail spikes correlate to GC pauses in controller (investigate).
- 2026-12-03: Load test day. Observed large cold-start penalty for KV cache; warm cache reduces p95 by ~30% after 10k queries.
- 2026-12-05: Canary 1% ramp. p50 stayed ~300ms, p95 hovered 1.1s; error-rate unchanged. Canary kept.
- 2026-12-06: Canary 5% ramp. On one node we saw repeated enqueue depth growth at peak; temporary autoscale prevented timeouts but increased cost by ~18%.
- 2026-12-07: Decision checkpoint: Balanced threshold (350ms p50 / 1.2s p95) passes usability and cost checks for short-chat with recommended mitigations: automatic cache warmers, soft-burst reserved nodes, and per-region guardrails.
- 2026-12-08: Draft runbook added and shared with infra and product for comments.

Outstanding questions / open issues:
- GC / controller pause root cause: is this a software bug or expected behavior under certain traffic patterns? (Action: Jordan to open infra ticket and attach flamegraphs).
- Token bucket for SDK: do we add client-side pacing to smooth spikes? (Priya to prototype).
- Should we define separate SLOs for Dedicated customers that pay for reserved capacity vs. hosted free-tier? (Decision: yes, different tiers — need contract language).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Choosing thresholds too tight triggers frequent rollbacks and ops churn. Mitigation: pick balanced initial thresholds and instrument error-budget burn alerts before changing SLO configs.
- Risk: Regional variance causes cross-region inconsistency. Mitigation: per-region baselines and gradual rollout with region-specific rollouts.
- Risk: Model upgrades change latency distribution. Mitigation: require SLO validation during model version onboarding with gated tests.

Rollout recommendation (high level):
- Phase 0 (staging): validate metrics collection + alerts (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (canary): per-region canary with 1% -> 15% ramp (2–3 weeks).
- Phase 2 (opt-in customers / Dedicated): offer opt-in threshold config for reserved capacity customers + contractual SLA discussions (3–6 weeks).
- Phase 3 (global): flip default for hosted API after sustained stability and stakeholder sign-off.

Owner matrix (who does what):
- Riley Chen (SRE): spike lead, decision owner, runbook author.
- Jordan Lee (serving-runtime): latency root cause analysis, kernel/queue suggestions.
- Priya Patel (observability): telemetry queries, dashboards, alert config.
- Ava Martinez (product): customer UX sign-off and priority routing requirements.
- Diego Alvarez (infra): autoscale policy adjustments and reserved pool feasibility.

Next actions (short list):
- Riley: finalize baseline charts and attach to this doc (due 2026-12-10).
- Jordan: open infra bug for GC pauses and link to this doc (due 2026-12-11).
- Priya: push a dashboard template and the prometheus queries to linked_artifacts (due 2026-12-12).
- Stakeholder sync: schedule 30m review with product + infra + serving on 2026-12-13.

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- Might be useful to capture perceived latency in SDK logs (client-observed) and correlate to our server-side telemetry — network noise can hide real regressions.
- If warm cache brings p95 under threshold, we should invest in light-weight TTL-based cache warmers rather than adding heavy reserved capacity.
- Keep decision log terse but linked to raw data snapshots (screenshot links + query ids).

Appendix (quick query snippets to run):
- promql: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, model_size))
- trace filter: trace.duration > 0.9s AND route =~ "/v1/chat" AND token_count <= 128

Status: draft — this doc is the working artifact for the spike. Add observations as you run tests; aim to merge into the canonical SLO playbook once final selection is made.
